generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential from 1, unique, NOT NULL; generated PKs start at max(existing_pk)+1 and increment; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Planned multiplicity: for each FK column, after the parent table is final, assign child rows to parent keys so that at least one parent has exactly 1 child, one has exactly 2, one has >=3, and exactly one parent key (chosen deterministically, not the last key) has 0 children; remaining children are distributed uniformly over the other parent keys. Plan is applied after PK/UNIQUE dedup of the child table and the appended row count is sized to leave room for the plan. NULL only if the column is nullable (5% of rows).
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer in [1, 10000]; boundary values at listed literals +/-1 when a per_column_exception names the column.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random token of 3-12 alphanumeric chars; 10% near-duplicate variants (case flip, one-char edit) of an existing value.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_text: Random sentence-like string up to 200 chars; 10% near-duplicate variants; when a per_column_exception names a duplicate_share, that share of values are exact duplicates of an existing value.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_enum: Uniform pick from the enum list in per_column_exceptions; no boundary or near-variant values are inserted into enum columns.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_numeric_string: Zero-padded 3-digit string '000'-'999'; boundary values at listed literals +/-1 as strings.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_card_number: 16-digit numeric string; boundary values at listed literals +/-1 as strings.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_address: Multi-line US-style address with street, city, state, ZIP.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Uniform timestamp in [2009-01-01, 2018-12-31]; boundary values at listed literals +/-1 day.
generic_sampling_rules.double_amount: Uniform in [0.01, 5000.00], 2 decimals; boundary values at listed literals +/-0.01.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, NULL share follows the compact database's share for that column (fallback 5% when unknown), with at least one NULL row per nullable column per instance; NOT NULL and primary-key columns never get NULL; rules and formulas constrain only non-NULL operands and a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule. NULL planting for amount/date columns runs BEFORE tie and different-values construction; the applied share per column is recorded in the output for audit.
generic_sampling_rules.construction_order: 1) fill parent tables (PKs, then non-FK columns, then plant NULLs); 2) fill child tables' non-FK columns and plant NULLs; 3) apply FK multiplicity plans after child PK/UNIQUE dedup; 4) apply ties_for_order_limit and rows_with_different_values jointly on the final non-NULL amount values; 5) apply semantic rules; 6) verify all constructed properties and report per-instance checks.

uncertainty: previous_transaction_id has no FK declared; treated as nullable free integer. other_customer_details, transaction_comment, other_transaction_details are 100% NULL in sample; generated with compact-share NULLs (fallback 5%) and random text otherwise. LIKE-pattern and substring boundary variants ('%Art%', '%art%', 'cott', 'u', 'U', '%Credit%', 'credit') are query-side variants and are not inserted as data values; only literal boundary values ('Art', 'art', 'Turcotte', 'turcotte', 'Credit', 'Debit') are inserted. table_sizes_per_instance refers to total rows per instance (compact rows plus generated rows); the program computes appended = target - compact_size. Enum columns contain only enum values. group_sizes, aggregate_boundary and unmatched_join_rows are constructed by the FK multiplicity planner (exactly one childless parent per dependency, plus parents with 1, 2 and >=3 children) applied after child PK dedup; aggregate_boundary on COUNT(*)/COUNT(DISTINCT card_id) is realized by the same planner. ties_for_order_limit and rows_with_different_values are constructed jointly: within each tying transaction_type group the target SUM is split into two distinct amounts per group so both the SUM tie and the >=2-distinct-amounts property hold; an assertion reports both per instance. NULL planting for amount/date columns precedes tie/different-values construction; applied NULL shares are recorded in the output. Rules date ordering and duplicate shares (20-50%) rest on only 8 sample rows and are weakly supported.
